transcription.text: Do you expect to ever see, have you ever seen an actual HP Agilent Keysight clone?
Like an, like an actual, do you expect to ever, like a 100% clone? It's got the badge
in everything. It pretends to be a Keysight. We haven't seen a 100% counterfeit. We have
seen in a few cases, I know in the power products, where someone took our PC board,
depopulated it, put it on a Xerox machine and copied the burner out, including our logo.
And they were so small, they were selling so few that we didn't go after them, but we
had several panels in that product, we could have taken them out very easily, but it wasn't
worth the cost. They weren't a threat. We have had other people do, you know, the front
panel looks identical to our product, but certainly the function, there's someone cloned
And the menus are, I did a video showing the difference between, they're practically identical.

are copyrighted, and they knew not to copy verbatim the help screen, so they changed
every first word, because that gets around the copyright. And inside, it's not the same
function, it's not the same. No, no, no, no, it's a totally different hub. But the front
panel, the screens, the menus, it's identical. And that was a very, very good user interface
for its time. Do you think there's possibly code copying going on there, or do they simply
write it from scratch and use it as a visual template? We see way, we see much less of
that, because that requires a lot of work. You're taking an assembly line, you've got
a product. Oh, you've got to disassemble it. Yeah, yeah, it's almost impossible to. It's
not impossible. Right, but it's a lot of liquid. You put enough monkeys in a typewriter, Shakespeare

when they probably could have spent it better developing their own product. But, you know,
sometimes that's what they want to do. I don't know who for me to question it. We're trying
to find ways to keep them from representing themselves as being us. That's really the
challenge. Got it. Is it flattering? Is part of it flattering? Oh, in your UI, it's so
good that they copied it. Sure, sure, it's flattering. You know, when Samsung copied
Apple, it was a little bit flattering. It was also, they lost market, they sued them

They created a lot of great concepts. So yeah, it's flattering, but that doesn't last very

scope in it? So we are doing that. Sure, a new scope, have a function. Oh yeah, yeah,

Do you think that's still the plate and still the case?

We're doing that.
Yeah, I know your scope, your educational scope.

Okay, so anything up to maybe Bluetooth 2.4 gig is possible?
That's on the edge.
What it requires is, because you can't buy A to Ds that go that fast. We develop our

It's all custom ASIC stuff.
That's right. We're doing that because the higher you go, the more you can do. You can

that are outside the frequency you're trying to digitize and they can overload the front
end.
Of course.
Effectively, when you have a down converter in the front end, it's tuned, so you take
out those other frequencies before they hit the A to D, so you can get better performance
with a down converter than you can with direct digital.
Got it.
Unless you put a pre-selector in front of the thing, which you might as well have a
down converter.
Yeah, exactly. So it's always going to be a trade-off.
It's always going to be a trade-off.
Right. So you need both. You almost need to have two different grades of instrument.

Right. True.

They're in the original form factor, yeah. Well, in a few years, the actual panel,
